name: Stargazing
summary: Learn the constellations, find planets and galaxies and star-hop across the night sky with binoculars.

name: Telescope Making
summary: Grind and polish your own mirror by hand, then build the telescope around it.

name: Satellite Spotting
summary: Predict and spot the ISS, Tiangong and Starlink trains as they glide across the twilight sky.

name: Aurora Hunting
summary: Read space-weather forecasts, find dark skies and catch the northern or southern lights.

name: Eclipse Chasing
summary: Travel to the path of totality for a few of the strangest minutes nature has to offer.
safety: Wear certified eclipse glasses at every partial stage. Remove them only during totality itself.

name: Solar Observing
summary: Watch sunspots and prominences change from day to day through a properly filtered telescope.
safety: Never point any optics at the Sun without a certified full-aperture solar filter. The eye damage is instant and permanent.

name: Radio Astronomy
summary: Detect the hydrogen line of the Milky Way and meteor echoes with a home-built antenna and an SDR.

name: Birdwatching
summary: Identify birds by sight and song, keep lists and learn where and when to find them.

name: Insect Study
summary: Find, identify and watch beetles, butterflies, dragonflies and the rest of the insect world.

name: Wild Plant ID
summary: Identify wildflowers, grasses and ferns by family features, using keys and a hand lens.

name: Tree Identification
summary: Name trees by leaf, bark, buds and silhouette in any season.

name: Mycology
summary: Study fungi through spore prints, microscopy and keys, and see the hidden kingdom under every forest.
safety: Never eat a wild mushroom unless an expert has confirmed the ID in person. Some deadly species look like edible ones.

name: Microscopy
summary: Explore pond water, pollen, crystals and cells with a home microscope, and photograph what you find.

name: Amateur Meteorology
summary: Run a home weather station, read synoptic charts and make your own forecasts.

name: Cloud Spotting
summary: Name the clouds overhead, from cirrus to mammatus, and read what they say about the weather.

name: Storm Chasing
summary: Forecast severe storms, then intercept and photograph supercells and lightning from a safe position.
safety: Learn with experienced chasers. Always keep an escape route, respect lightning and never drive into flooded roads or the storm's path.

name: Geology
summary: Read landscapes and rock layers to see how mountains, coasts and valleys formed over millions of years.
safety: Wear eye protection when hammering rock, and keep away from unstable faces.

name: Fossil Hunting
summary: Find ammonites, shark teeth and trilobites on beaches and in quarries, and learn which rocks hide them.
safety: Check tide times, and stay away from cliff bases because rockfalls happen without warning.

name: Archaeology
summary: Volunteer on real excavations, then learn to read pottery, layers and landscapes for traces of the past.
safety: Dig only on supervised, permitted excavations. Disturbing protected sites or removing artefacts is illegal in most countries.

name: Rockpooling
summary: Explore rock pools at low tide for crabs, anemones, starfish and nudibranchs.
safety: Watch the incoming tide and swell. Turn rocks back over gently and return animals where you found them.

name: Citizen Science
summary: Contribute real data to research by counting birds, classifying galaxies or logging wildlife sightings.

name: Nature Journaling
summary: Sketch, note and wonder about what you see outdoors, mixing words, pictures and numbers on the page.

name: Field Recording
summary: Capture dawn choruses, city ambience and hidden sounds with portable recorders and hydrophones.

name: Kitchen Chemistry
summary: Run real experiments with household ingredients, from colour-changing cabbage indicator to elephant toothpaste.
safety: Wear eye protection, follow tested recipes and never mix cleaning products.

name: Crystal Growing
summary: Grow large single crystals from saturated solutions by controlling seeds, temperature and patience.
safety: Some salts, such as copper sulfate, are toxic. Keep them away from food and small children.

name: Model Rocketry
summary: Build and launch rockets on solid motors, add altimeters and cameras, and recover them by parachute.
safety: Use only certified motors, follow the model rocketry safety code and launch in open fields with the landowner's permission.

name: Genealogy
summary: Trace your family tree through records, archives and DNA, and uncover the stories behind the names.

name: Science Communication
summary: Explain science through talks, videos and writing so that it is accurate and genuinely exciting.

name: Bat Detecting
summary: Hear bats' ultrasonic calls with a detector and identify species by sound at dusk.
safety: Don't handle bats. Some carry rabies or related viruses, so call a bat rescue for grounded bats.

name: Whale Watching
summary: Spot whales, dolphins and seabirds from headlands and boats, and learn to read the signs at sea.

name: Herping
summary: Find wild reptiles and amphibians such as newts, lizards and snakes, and photograph them in their habitat.
safety: Never handle venomous species, and check local laws. Many reptiles and amphibians are protected.

name: Moth Trapping
summary: Run a light trap overnight, then identify the surprisingly beautiful moths at dawn and let them go.

name: Plant Breeding
summary: Cross-pollinate plants by hand to create your own varieties of tomato, dahlia or chilli.
